Find, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD.$
question.worked_solution:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{BD}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△CBD$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226856/assets/da5c25d9e1e54a79b8e2c8532d4571dd42ccd4e6e6a3fa69aa1fc9075c19b39d.png)

 Computing the area of $△CBD,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{CBD} & =\frac{1}{2}(21)(12)\operatorname{sin}⁡{66}^{∘} \\  & =126\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{66}^{∘} \\  & ≈115.107,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{CBD} \\  & =2\cdot 115.107 \\  & =230.214.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, to the nearest integer, the area of the parallelogram is $230.$
